draft.title: Drugs in sport
card: The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) sets the list of substances and methods banned in sport. Athletes who use them break the rules and can face penalties.
Anabolic steroids are banned. They act like male sex hormones and build muscle mass, so an athlete can train harder and get stronger.
EPO is banned. It raises the number of red blood cells, so the blood carries more oxygen to the muscles, which helps endurance.
WADA gives two main reasons for banning them. They can harm the health of the athlete, and they give an unfair advantage over athletes who follow the rules.
draft.remember: Banned drugs are on the list because they risk health and make competition unfair.

a.q: Which pair of reasons best explains why WADA bans substances such as EPO?
opts: They can harm health and give an unfair advantage
They are costly and make training sessions harder
They are new and have not yet been tested by athletes
They slow recovery and lower the athlete's performance
a.why: The card gives two reasons: harm to health and an unfair advantage over others. The last option is tempting, but banned drugs are used because they improve performance, not lower it.
a.clue: Think about the athlete's body and the other competitors.

b.q: Tom, a distance runner, says EPO should be banned only because it is unsafe, and that if it were safe it would be fair to use. Why is he wrong, using the card?
opts: It would still give an unfair advantage over rule followers
It would still be banned only if it built muscle mass
It would still be allowed because it is not a steroid
It would still be a risk to rivals who do not use it
b.why: WADA bans these substances for two reasons, and unfair advantage is separate from health harm. A safe drug that raised oxygen delivery would still give an edge over athletes who follow the rules. Being a steroid is not what makes a substance banned.
b.clue: WADA gives two reasons, not one.

a.best: They can harm health and give an unfair advantage

b.best: It would still give an unfair advantage over rule followers

problems.detail: The card says WADA gives 'two main reasons' for a ban. WADA's Code actually lists three criteria: it can enhance performance, it is an actual or potential health risk, and it violates the spirit of sport. A substance or method is listed if it meets any two. Calling health and unfair advantage WADA's two reasons oversimplifies this. A safer wording is 'Two key reasons for banning them are...'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The only concern is that the card presents 'two main reasons' as WADA's own position, when WADA uses three criteria and lists a substance that meets any two; consider rewording.
